reader.requirement: When neither GR17 overflow condition occurs (pointer within 1..size at initiation, and no unexamined sender characters once every receiver is acted upon), after the transfers the ON OVERFLOW imperative must be skipped and control go to the end of the statement or to the NOT ON OVERFLOW imperative, honouring an explicit transfer of control inside it.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.UnstringZeroLengthSenderTerminates: the 2002+ zero-length-sender guard is not emitted at 85; the GR17a pointer test is emitted only with a POINTER phrase (kb/Work PB5858)
EC-OVERFLOW-UNSTRING raise only where >>TURN enabled it; never at 85

reader.edition-search: grep of StringEmitter.cs and EcEmitter.cs for DialectBehaviors|Edition|DialectLevel
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the not-overflow dispatch; the zero-length sender guard is 2002+ only
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c35_unstring_not_on_overflow covers the plain no-overflow case; a boundary pointer, an exact fit, a trailing delimiter, ALL, an exhausted sender, an ODO sender, a ref-mod receiver, a signed-separate receiver and GO TO in the NOT phrase are not exercised

probes.printed: T10 NOOVF 7XYZWQCCC; T11 NOOVF 3XYZWQ (ODO group sender at 7 and 3 occurrences); T3 NOOVF C 12 (pointer = size); T9 NOOVF (ref-mod receiver B(1:2))
probes.expected: no overflow; the NOT ON OVERFLOW imperative executed

probes.printed: T1 AAABBBCCC (ON OVERFLOW only, ignored); T2 GOTO OK (GO TO in NOT ON OVERFLOW); T4/T5/T7/T8 NOOVF (exact fit, trailing delimiter, ALL delimiter, sender exhausted with D not acted upon, tally 03); T15 NOOVF P=12 / T15 STILL (IF inside imperative-statement-2)
probes.expected: GR20: ON OVERFLOW ignored, NOT ON OVERFLOW or the end of the statement

probes.printed: T6 OVF (one character after the last delimiter); T12 OVF 123+ (signed separate, size-1 examined); T13 OVF (pointer 12 > 11); T14 OVF 05
probes.expected: GR17 overflow, so GR20 does not apply (contrast)

probes.printed: COBOL0900 at 85 for NOT ON OVERFLOW written before ON OVERFLOW

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR20  the text is in the clause or rule: "if the NOT ON OVERFLOW phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-2"
OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR17  the text is in the clause or rule: "causes an overflow condition"

reader.notes: The overflow flag is set only by the GR17a pointer test and the GR17b unexamined-characters test; EmitPair runs the NOT imperative exactly when the flag is clear. A reference-modified identifier-1 is refused at 85 (§1985:VI.6.27.3 SR7), so a ref-mod receiver stood in for class a beside the ODO sender.

refuter.evidence: Probe ru1.cob at --std 85 (runs/ru1-002): pointer 0 and pointer -1 (signed pointer) both overflow, NOT phrase skipped (U4 OVF PT0 +00, U5 OVF PTNEG); 'AAA,,' DELIMITED BY ',' into one receiver overflows (U6, second delimiter unexamined) while DELIMITED BY ALL ',' does not (U7 NOOVF AAA); no DELIMITED BY, sender exactly filling two receivers: no overflow (U8 NOOVF ABCDEF), into one shorter receiver: overflow (U9 OVF ABC); POINTER 5 on a 6-character sender into a 3-character receiver: no overflow, pointer 7 (U10 NOOVF EF +07).
